ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached Lewis diagram shows nitric acid as resonance structures. In each structure, N is the central atom bonded to three O atoms. One O is bonded to H, forming an H–O–N connection. The other two O atoms are bonded to N, with one N–O bond drawn as a double bond and the other as a single bond in each resonance form. No lone pairs are shown on the central N, so around N there are three bonding regions and zero lone-pair regions. Reasoning: The question asks what statement about HNO3 follows from this Lewis diagram. By VSEPR theory, a central atom with three electron domains and no lone pairs has trigonal planar geometry. Therefore the atoms around nitrogen lie in one plane, so nitric acid molecules are planar.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: note that the diagram shows resonance, with a double bond to one terminal oxygen in one structure and to the other terminal oxygen in the second structure. Use the text to confirm this is nitric acid, HNO3. Interpret the resonance as delocalization of pi bonding over the N-O framework. Since effective pi delocalization requires aligned p orbitals, the N and O atoms adopt an sp2-like coplanar arrangement. Therefore the true statement is that HNO3 molecules are planar.

In the right structure, the N=O double bond is instead to the right terminal O, while the upper O is singly bonded to N. Reasoning: These resonance forms indicate that pi bonding is delocalized over the N-O framework. Effective pi delocalization requires overlapping, aligned p orbitals, so the N and O atoms adopt an sp2-like coplanar arrangement. Therefore the true statement is that nitric acid molecules are planar.
